# Data and packages

```{r packages}
library(tidyverse)
library(lme4)
library(car)
library(emmeans)
```

```{r data}
data <- read.csv("data/data2.csv", sep = ";", na.strings = "NA") %>%
  mutate(Mite_ID = factor(Mite_ID),
         # growth between measurements
         H1_H2 = P_height_2 - P_height,
         H2_H3 = P_height_3 - P_height_2,
         L1_L2 = P_leaves_2 - P_leaves,
         L2_L3 = P_leaves_3 - P_leaves_2,
         P1_P2 = P_pistil_VIZ_2 - P_pistil_VIZ,
         P2_P3 = P_pistil_VIZ_3 - P_pistil_VIZ_2)
```

# Data preparation

Plants were measured at three time points (weeks 4, 6 and 7). The data are
reshaped from one row per plant to one row per plant per time point.

```{r reshape}
# Measurements from one time point (n = 1, 2 or 3)
timepoint <- function(n, week) {
  sfx <- if (n == 1) "" else paste0("_", n)
  data.frame(
    ID = data$ID, Block = data$Block, Pot = data$Pot, Plant = data$Plant,
    Nutrient = data$Nutrient, Mite_ID = data$Mite_ID, Replica = data$Replica,
    Ecosystem = data$Ecosystem,
    Date   = data[[paste0("Date_", n)]],
    Leaves = data[[paste0("P_leaves", sfx)]],
    Height = data[[paste0("P_height", sfx)]],
    Pistil = data[[paste0("P_pistil_VIZ", sfx)]],
    Mites  = data[[paste0("Mite_N", sfx)]],
    Week   = week
  )
}

d1 <- timepoint(1, "W4")
d2 <- timepoint(2, "W6")
d3 <- timepoint(3, "W7")

# All time points (used for descriptive plots)
dt <- bind_rows(d1, d2, d3) %>% mutate(Week = factor(Week))

# Weeks 6 and 7, with week-4 values as the initial (baseline) measurement
dt2 <- bind_rows(d2, d3)
baseline <- d1 %>% select(ID, InLeaves = Leaves, InHeight = Height)
dt3 <- inner_join(dt2, baseline, by = "ID")

# Only plants that received mites
dt_mites <- dt3 %>% filter(Mite_ID != "No")

# Total mites per pot, for plants with mites
count_block <- data %>%
  filter(Mite_ID != "No") %>%
  group_by(Block, Mite_ID, Nutrient, Ecosystem, Pot) %>%
  summarise(Mite_total2 = sum(Mite_N_2),
            Mite_total3 = sum(Mite_N_3),
            .groups = "drop")
```

```{r helpers}
# Histogram + Shapiro-Wilk test
check_normality <- function(x, title, xlab) {
  hist(x, main = title, xlab = xlab)
  shapiro.test(x)
}

# Estimated marginal means with 95% CI, one panel per level of `panel`
mite_colours <- c("#00BFC4", "#F8766D", "#7CAE00", "#C77CFF", "#FFC300")

plot_emmeans <- function(means, x, panel, ylab, dodge = -0.2) {
  ggplot(means, aes(x = .data[[x]], y = emmean, group = .data[[panel]])) +
    facet_wrap(reformulate(panel), ncol = 4) +
    geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lower.CL, ymax = upper.CL), colour = "black",
                  width = 0, linewidth = 0.75, alpha = 0.66,
                  position = position_dodge(dodge)) +
    geom_line() +
    geom_point(aes(fill = Mite_ID), shape = 21, size = 2.5, stroke = 1,
               position = position_dodge(dodge)) +
    ylab(ylab) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = mite_colours) +
    theme_bw() + theme(aspect.ratio = 1)
}
```

# Data distribution

## Height

```{r}
check_normality(data$P_height,   "Initial plant height",      "Initial height (mm)")
check_normality(data$P_height_2, "Intermediate plant height", "Intermediate height (mm)")
check_normality(data$H1_H2,      "Growth between measurements 1 and 2", "H2 - H1 (mm)")
```

None of the height variables are normally distributed.

## Leaves

```{r}
check_normality(data$P_leaves,   "Initial number of leaves",      "Initial leaves")
check_normality(data$P_leaves_2, "Intermediate number of leaves", "Intermediate leaves")
check_normality(data$L1_L2,      "Leaf change between measurements 1 and 2", "L2 - L1")
```

None of the leaf variables are normally distributed.

# Models

All models are linear mixed-effects models with week nested within ecosystem as
random effects, tested with Type III F-tests.

**Note on main effects.** With R's default treatment contrasts, the Type III test of a
main effect in a model with an interaction tests that effect at the reference level of
the other factor only (bean mites for fertiliser, control plants for mite origin). The
overall effects below are therefore taken from estimated marginal means (`emmeans`):
the effect is first estimated in each group, and the average effect is the mean of
those group effects. Each model shows this calculation step by step.

## Height

**Model 1:** Height ~ Initial height + Nutrient × Mite origin + (1 | Week/Ecosystem)

```{r}
model1 <- lmer(Height ~ InHeight + Nutrient * Mite_ID + (1 | Week/Ecosystem), data = dt3)
Anova(model1, type = "III", test.statistic = "F")
summary(model1)

means_height <- as.data.frame(emmeans(model1, specs = pairwise ~ Nutrient * Mite_ID)$emmeans)
means_height

# 1. Effect in each group
by_group <- as.data.frame(pairs(emmeans(model1, ~ Nutrient | Mite_ID)))
by_group$effect <- -by_group$estimate
by_group[, c("Mite_ID", "effect", "p.value")]

# 2. Average effect by hand: the mean of the group effects
mean(by_group$effect)

# 3. The same average with emmeans, which also gives the P value
pairs(emmeans(model1, ~ Nutrient))
```

**Results**

* Initial height: P < 2e-16 (estimate = 0.717)
* Fertiliser within each mite group: +20.4 mm with bean mites (P = 0.015),
  +16.6 mm with tomato mites (P = 0.045), +12.8 mm without mites (P = 0.12)
* Fertiliser, averaged over mite groups: (20.4 + 16.6 + 12.8) / 3 = +16.6 mm (P = 0.0008)
* Fertiliser × mite origin: not significant (P = 0.80)

**Conclusion.** Plants that started taller stayed taller: each extra mm of
initial height predicted about 0.7 mm more height later. Fertiliser increased
height by about 17 mm on average compared with control plants.

From the plots, plants with mites from tomato were the smallest and plants with
mites from bean the tallest. Mites from tomato may be more costly to the plant.

```{r}
plot_emmeans(means_height, x = "Nutrient", panel = "Mite_ID",
             ylab = "Height in mm (estimated marginal means)")
plot_emmeans(means_height, x = "Mite_ID", panel = "Nutrient",
             ylab = "Height in mm (estimated marginal means)")
```

## Leaves

**Model 2:** Leaves ~ Initial leaves + Nutrient × Mite origin + (1 | Week/Ecosystem)

```{r}
model2 <- lmer(Leaves ~ InLeaves + Nutrient * Mite_ID + (1 | Week/Ecosystem), data = dt3)
Anova(model2, type = "III", test.statistic = "F")
summary(model2)

means_leaves <- as.data.frame(emmeans(model2, specs = pairwise ~ Nutrient * Mite_ID)$emmeans)
means_leaves

# Fertiliser effect within each mite group (the interaction is significant)
pairs(emmeans(model2, ~ Nutrient | Mite_ID))
```

**Results**

* Initial leaves: P = 6.4e-05 (estimate = 0.27)
* Fertiliser × mite origin: P = 0.0095 (df = 2)
* Fertiliser within each mite group: +2.2 leaves without mites (P < 0.0001),
  +1.2 with bean mites (P = 0.0008), +0.8 with tomato mites (P = 0.024)

**Conclusion.** Plants with more leaves at the start kept having more leaves
(about 0.3 more per initial leaf). Fertilised plants had more leaves in every
mite group, but the size of the effect depended on mite origin: about 2.2 more
leaves without mites, 1.2 with bean mites and 0.8 with tomato mites. The largest fertiliser effect was in plants without mites,
which suggests that mites may counteract the benefit of fertiliser.

```{r}
plot_emmeans(means_leaves, x = "Nutrient", panel = "Mite_ID",
             ylab = "Total leaves (estimated marginal means)")
plot_emmeans(means_leaves, x = "Mite_ID", panel = "Nutrient",
             ylab = "Total leaves (estimated marginal means)")
```

## Pistils

**Model 3:** Pistils ~ Nutrient × Mite origin + (1 | Week/Ecosystem)

```{r}
model3 <- lmer(Pistil ~ Nutrient * Mite_ID + (1 | Week/Ecosystem), data = dt3,
               control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa"))
Anova(model3, type = "III", test.statistic = "F")
summary(model3)

means_pistil <- as.data.frame(emmeans(model3, specs = pairwise ~ Nutrient * Mite_ID)$emmeans)
means_pistil

# 1. Effect in each group
by_group <- as.data.frame(pairs(emmeans(model3, ~ Nutrient | Mite_ID)))
by_group$effect <- -by_group$estimate
by_group[, c("Mite_ID", "effect", "p.value")]

# 2. Average effect by hand: the mean of the group effects
mean(by_group$effect)

# 3. The same average with emmeans, which also gives the P value
pairs(emmeans(model3, ~ Nutrient))
```

**Results**

* Fertiliser within each mite group: +2.725 with bean mites (P = 0.004),
  +1.567 with tomato mites (P = 0.090), +2.167 without mites (P = 0.021)
* Fertiliser, averaged over mite groups: (2.725 + 1.567 + 2.167) / 3 = +2.15 pistils (P = 0.0001)
* Fertiliser × mite origin: not significant (P = 0.67)

**Conclusion.** Fertilised plants had about 2 more pistils than control plants,
which suggests a higher potential reproductive output.

```{r}
plot_emmeans(means_pistil, x = "Nutrient", panel = "Mite_ID",
             ylab = "Total pistils (estimated marginal means)")
plot_emmeans(means_pistil, x = "Mite_ID", panel = "Nutrient",
             ylab = "Total pistils (estimated marginal means)")
```

## Mites

**Model 4:** Mites ~ Nutrient × Mite origin + (1 | Week/Ecosystem), plants with mites only

```{r}
model4 <- lmer(Mites ~ Nutrient * Mite_ID + (1 | Week/Ecosystem), data = dt_mites)
Anova(model4, type = "III", test.statistic = "F")
summary(model4)

means_mites <- as.data.frame(emmeans(model4, specs = pairwise ~ Nutrient * Mite_ID)$emmeans)
means_mites

# 1. Effect in each group
by_group <- as.data.frame(pairs(emmeans(model4, ~ Mite_ID | Nutrient)))
by_group$effect <- by_group$estimate
by_group[, c("Nutrient", "effect", "p.value")]

# 2. Average effect by hand: the mean of the group effects
mean(by_group$effect)

# 3. The same average with emmeans, which also gives the P value
pairs(emmeans(model4, ~ Mite_ID))

# Fertiliser averaged over mite origin
pairs(emmeans(model4, ~ Nutrient))
```

**Results**

* Mite origin within each fertiliser group: 2.04 fewer tomato than bean mites in control
  plants (P = 0.052), 2.45 fewer in fertilised plants (P = 0.021)
* Mite origin, averaged over fertiliser: (2.04 + 2.45) / 2 = 2.25 fewer tomato mites (P = 0.0035)
* Fertiliser, averaged over mite origin: no effect (P = 0.14)
* Fertiliser × mite origin: not significant (P = 0.78)

**Conclusion.** Plants carried about 2 fewer mites from tomato than from bean.
Fertiliser did not change the number of mites. The Type III test of mite origin
(P = 0.052) only compares the two origins in control plants, which is why it looked
borderline.

```{r}
plot_emmeans(means_mites, x = "Nutrient", panel = "Mite_ID",
             ylab = "Number of mites (estimated marginal means)")
plot_emmeans(means_mites, x = "Mite_ID", panel = "Nutrient",
             ylab = "Number of mites (estimated marginal means)")
```

# Descriptive plots

```{r}
boxplot_by_week <- function(df, y, fill = NULL) {
  mapping <- if (is.null(fill)) aes(x = Nutrient, y = .data[[y]])
             else aes(x = Nutrient, y = .data[[y]], fill = .data[[fill]])
  ggplot(df, mapping) +
    geom_boxplot() +
    facet_grid(cols = vars(Week))
}

boxplot_by_week(dt,  "Height")
boxplot_by_week(dt,  "Height", fill = "Mite_ID")
boxplot_by_week(dt,  "Leaves")
boxplot_by_week(dt,  "Leaves", fill = "Mite_ID")
boxplot_by_week(dt2, "Pistil")
boxplot_by_week(dt2, "Pistil", fill = "Mite_ID")
boxplot_by_week(dt2, "Mites")
boxplot_by_week(dt2, "Mites",  fill = "Mite_ID")
```

```{r}
ggplot(count_block, aes(x = Nutrient, y = Mite_total2)) +
  geom_boxplot() + facet_grid(cols = vars(Mite_ID)) +
  ylab("Total mites per pot (measurement 2)")

ggplot(count_block, aes(x = Nutrient, y = Mite_total3)) +
  geom_boxplot() + facet_grid(cols = vars(Mite_ID)) +
  ylab("Total mites per pot (measurement 3)")
```
